subject: Maths
subtopic: Surface area of cylinders and spheres
title: Surface area of cylinders and spheres
subtitle: Volume and Surface Area · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can calculate the surface area of cylinders and spheres using formulae.

key_vocab.definition: The surface area of a 3D shape is the total area of all its faces. A cylinder has two circular ends and a curved surface that unfolds into a rectangle. A sphere has a single curved surface.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can calculate the surface area of cylinders and spheres using formulae.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: surface area -- The surface area of a 3D shape is the total area of all its faces. A cylinder has two circular ends and a curved surface that unfolds into a rectangle. A sphere has a single curved surface.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Surface area is the total area covering the outside of a 3D shape. Use the correct formula for each shape.
Cylinder SA = 2πr² + 2πrh
Two circular ends plus the curved surface area

Key examples:
  ✓ Cylinder: 2πr² + 2πrh  (two circles plus curved surface)
  ✓ Sphere: 4πr²  (four times the area of a great circle)
  ✓ Curved surface of cylinder = 2πrh  (rectangle when unrolled)
  ✗ Cylinder SA = πr²h  (that is the volume formula)
  ✗ Sphere SA = 2πr²  (must be 4πr²)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – cylinder surface area
  Find the surface area of a cylinder with radius 5 cm and height 8 cm. Give your answer to 1 d.p.
  Two circles: 2πr² = 2 × π × 5² = 50π
  Curved surface: 2πrh = 2 × π × 5 × 8 = 80π
  Total = 50π + 80π = 130π = 408.4 cm²
  408.4 cm²
  (Add the area of both circles and the curved surface.)

Example 2 – sphere surface area
  Find the surface area of a sphere with radius 6 cm. Give your answer to 1 d.p.
  SA = 4πr²
  = 4 × π × 6²
  = 144π = 452.4 cm²
  452.4 cm²
  (Substitute the radius into 4πr².)

sections.title: Cylinder surface area
sections.content:
Find the total surface area of each cylinder. Round to 1 d.p.

(a) r = 3 cm, h = 7 cm
(b) r = 4 cm, h = 10 cm
(c) r = 2 cm, h = 9 cm
(d) r = 6 cm, h = 5 cm

sections.title: Sphere surface area
sections.content:

(b) r = 3 cm

(d) r = 7 cm

sections.title: Hemispheres
sections.content:

(b) r = 8 cm

(d) r = 6 cm

sections.title: Open cylinders
sections.content:
Find the surface area of each open-top cylinder. Round to 1 d.p.

(a) r = 4 cm, h = 6 cm
(b) r = 5 cm, h = 12 cm
(c) r = 3 cm, h = 8 cm
(d) r = 7 cm, h = 4 cm

sections.title: Mixed problems
sections.content:
Solve each surface area problem. Round to 1 d.p.

(a) Cylinder: r = 2.5 cm, h = 6 cm. Total SA?
(b) Sphere with diameter 14 cm. SA?
(c) Hemisphere: r = 9 cm. Total SA?
(d) Cylinder with no ends: r = 4 cm, h = 10 cm. Curved SA?
(e) Sphere with circumference 31.4 cm. Find r, then SA.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Cylinder SA = 2πr² + 2πrh includes both circles and the curved surface
✗ Sphere SA = 2πr²
✓ The curved surface area of a cylinder equals 2πrh
✗ A hemisphere has surface area exactly half of a full sphere
✓ Surface area is always measured in square units
